definitions.explanation: A fixed expression whose meaning cannot be fully understood from the individual words alone. Used as a linguistic term when discussing language and grammar.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{慣用語|かんようご}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{意味|いみ}→意味：01155_imi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{教|おし}えて→教える：00526_oshieru⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please tell me the meaning of this idiom.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{体|からだ}→体：00784_karada⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{関|かん}する→関する：02045_kansuru⟧{慣用語|かんようご}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: There are many body-related idioms in Japanese.

examples.japanese: {慣用語|かんようご}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{正|ただ}しく⟦{使|つか}える→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦ようになる→ようになる：28408_youninaru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧より⟦{自然|しぜん}→自然：01423_shizen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{聞|き}こえる→聞こえる：01229_kikoeru⟧。
examples.english: Once you can use idioms correctly, your Japanese will sound more natural.

notes:
A linguistic term for fixed expressions whose meaning goes beyond the literal words. Japanese is particularly rich in body-part idioms (⟦{体|からだ}→体：00784_karada⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{慣用語|かんようご}), such as ⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧ (to have a good eye), ⟦{手|て}を{焼|や}く→手を焼く：07438_tewoyaku⟧ (to have difficulty with), and ⟦{腹|はら}が{立|た}つ→腹が立つ：06886_haragatatsu⟧ (to get angry).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {慣用語|かんようご}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{覚|おぼ}える→覚える：00739_oboeru⟧: to learn idioms
- {慣用語|かんようご}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{意味|いみ}→意味：01155_imi⟧: meaning of an idiom
- ⟦{体|からだ}→体：00784_karada⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{慣用語|かんようご}: body-part idioms
- {慣用語|かんようご}⟦{辞典|じてん}→辞典：01640_jiten⟧: idiom dictionary

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{慣用句|かんようく}→慣用句：15890_kanyouku⟧: idiomatic phrase — often used interchangeably, but ⟦{慣用句|かんようく}→慣用句：15890_kanyouku⟧ specifically refers to phrasal units, while {慣用語|かんようご} can include single idiomatic words
- ⟦{諺|ことわざ}→諺：02765_kotowaza⟧: proverb — a complete sentence expressing traditional wisdom, not the same as an idiom
